name: Basic Walk
description: Ground-based locomotion with configurable speed and acceleration. Movement CONTINUES while a direction is held rather than advancing once per press, because `input.moveDirection` reports whether the key is still down and a body that ignores that makes the player tap to walk. It also accepts `input.faceDirection`, which turns without moving, and `input.aim`, which points the body continuously at a screen position so an attack can be swung or fired along the exact bearing rather than snapped to one of four — the aim half of a twin-stick or the look half of a shoulder-button strafe, and the thing a player needs when the swing scans the way they are pointed and they do not want to step into what they are hitting. It also names itself: `unitId` is the id this body answers to on the board, and a successful step is announced as `movement.moveExecuted` — the same event a tactical move uses. That is what lets a real-time player character BE a unit in combat.unit_roster rather than a second, parallel position nothing else can see. Without it a build has a walker the enemies cannot find and a roster entry that never moves, and the pursuers converge on a phantom.

implementations.note: Implemented in the consuming application; not verifiable from this repository.

inputs.name: startX
inputs.description: Where the body begins along X, in tiles. Null means the middle of the board. A region entered by walking off a neighbour should begin at the border it was entered THROUGH, not at the centre, or every crossing teleports the player away from the place they were walking toward.

inputs.name: startY
inputs.description: The same along Y. Null means the middle.

inputs.name: unitId
inputs.description: The id this body answers to on the board. A step is announced as movement.moveExecuted carrying it, so a combat.unit_roster holding a unit of the same id tracks the player exactly as it tracks a tactical unit — and the player then has health, a team, and a place in everything that reads the roster, for free. A build with no roster ignores the event and nothing changes.

outputs.name: isMoving
outputs.description: Whether the character is currently moving

outputs.name: aimAngle
outputs.description: Where the body is pointed, in radians, measured from due east and increasing clockwise on screen. `input.aim` sets it continuously — a mouse, a stick — while `input.faceDirection` and `input.moveDirection` snap it to the nearest quarter turn. A component that swings along a line needs the angle; one that picks a sprite needs the quarter turn; both are the same fact at different resolutions, which is why this is published beside the four-way facing rather than instead of it.
